q-78011.name: Question 3
q-78011.problem: Margaret is studying and analyzing a culture of bacteria. From a certain moment, she notices that the number of bacteria $B(t)$ in the culture grows according to the formula $B(t)=500\cdot {2}^{t},$ where $t$ denotes the time in hours. How many bacteria will there be after $4$ hours?
q-78011.worked_solution:
To get the number of bacteria in the culture after $4$ hours, we evaluate the function at $t=4.$ Substituting $t=4$ into the function $B(t)$ gives

$$
\begin{aligned}B(t) & =500\cdot (2)^{(4)} \\  & =500\cdot 16 \\  & =8\,000.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, there will be $8\,000$ bacteria in the culture after $4$ hours.

q-45715.name: Question 4
q-45715.problem: The population $Z(t)$ of zebras in a certain nature reserve is given by $Z(t)=10\,000\cdot (1.2)^{t}$, where $t$ is the time in years since the reserve was opened. How many zebras will be in the reserve after $4$ years?
q-45715.worked_solution:
To get the number of zebras after $4$ years, we evaluate the function at $t=4.$ Substituting $t=4$ into the function $Z(t)$ gives

$$
\begin{aligned}Z & =10\,000\cdot (1.2)^{(4)} \\  & =10\,000\cdot 2.073\,6 \\  & =20\,736.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, after $4$ years, there will be $20\,736$ zebras in the nature reserve.

q-64042.name: Question 7
q-64042.worked_solution:
First, we substitute $g(t)=80$ into the equation:

$$
5\cdot {4}^{t}=80
$$

We can divide both sides of the equation by the constant factor of $5:$

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{5\cdot {4}^{t}}{5} & =\frac{80}{5} \\ \frac{\cancel{5}\cdot {4}^{t}}{\cancel{5}} & =16 \\ {4}^{t} & =16\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we solve for $t$ using the fact that $16$ is a power of $4:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{4}^{t} & ={4}^{2} \\ t & =2\end{aligned}
$$

First, we substitute $h(t)=320$ into the equation:

$$
5\cdot {4}^{3t+6}=320
$$

We can divide both sides of the equation by the constant factor of $5:$

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{5\cdot {4}^{3t+6}}{5} & =\frac{320}{5} \\ \frac{\cancel{5}\cdot {4}^{3t+6}}{\cancel{5}} & =64 \\ {4}^{3t+6} & =64\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we solve for $t$ using the fact that $64$ is a power of $4:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{4}^{3t+6} & ={4}^{3} \\ 3t+6 & =3 \\ 3t & =-3 \\ t & =-1\end{aligned}
$$
